Recall Timing and Tempo

When you go back to base matters as much as what you buy. Good recalls keep you strong, safe and on time for objectives.

Why recall timing matters

Every time you recall, you leave the map for 30-40 seconds: 8 seconds of channel, time in base, and the walk back. If you pick the wrong moment, you lose minions, experience, turret plates or an objective. If you pick the right moment, you come back with an item spike while your opponent is still in lane with old items.

This idea of using your time well is called tempo. A player with good tempo is always in the right place at the right time: shopping when nothing is happening, and back on the map when it matters.

The three questions before you recall

  1. Where is the wave? The ideal recall is right after you crash a wave into the enemy tower. See Wave Management: Push, Freeze and Crash.
  2. How much gold do you have? Back when you can buy something meaningful, like a component that completes part of your item.
  3. What's coming up? If a dragon spawns in 60 seconds, recall now so you're back in time, not right as the fight starts.
Pro tipCheck the dragon and Void Grub timers before your first recall. Coming back with a fresh item just as an objective spawns is how lanes win fights for their jungler.

Good gold amounts to recall with

You don't need to memorize every item cost, but a few numbers help. These are good first-recall targets:

Champion typeGood buy
Mage (mid)Lost Chapter (mana and haste) or Blasting Wand for damage
Marksman (bot)B. F. Sword or a damage component like Pickaxe
AnyoneBoots plus a Control Ward if you're short on gold

The exact item depends on your build (check your champion's guide). The idea is to avoid recalling with tiny amounts of gold unless you have to, and to avoid staying in lane with 2000+ unspent gold while your opponent is already stronger.

Always grab a Control Ward when you have 75 spare gold. It's the cheapest way to make your lane safer.

When you have to recall early

Sometimes you're low on health or mana and the wave is in a bad spot. Here's how to decide:

  • If you'll die by staying, recall. A death costs far more than a lost wave: your opponent gets 300+ gold and you lose even more time.
  • If you're just a bit low, try to push one more wave first, then recall.
  • If the wave is about to crash into your tower, the tower will kill a lot of it. You lose some gold, but turret plates can take damage. Since plates are permanent now, losing a plate means the enemy keeps that gold advantage for the rest of the game.
Common mistakeRecalling in the middle of the lane where the enemy can see you. Recall in a safe spot (behind your tower or in a brush) so nobody interrupts your 8-second channel.

Syncing recalls with your team

Recalls work best when they line up with your team:

  • With your jungler: if your jungler is about to fight for an objective, recall a bit earlier so you can arrive with full health and an item.
  • In bot lane: the ADC and support should usually recall together. If one stays alone, they're easy to dive.
  • After a kill: if you just killed your opponent, use their death time to push the wave and recall. You'll come back stronger with no farm lost.
  • When the enemy recalls: if your opponent recalls and you have the wave, you can push it to their tower and take a plate, or recall at the same time to stay even.

Walking back

The walk back to lane is part of your recall. Use it well:

  • Place a ward on the way, especially near river brush or the jungle entrance closest to your lane.
  • Look at the minimap. If your jungler is nearby and the enemy laner is pushed up, you might arrive for a gank.
  • Take the safe path. Walking through an unwarded enemy jungle alone is a common way to die.

Key takeaways

  • The best time to recall is right after crashing a wave into the enemy tower.
  • Back with enough gold to buy something meaningful, and grab a Control Ward.
  • If staying means dying, recall. A death costs more than a wave.
  • Time recalls so you're back for objectives, not arriving late.
  • Plates are permanent now, so letting waves hit your tower while you're away costs more.
